question: Presidency College, established in 1817 as the Hindu College, is located in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kolkata.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Presidency College is located at Kolkata. It was founded in 1817 as the Hindu College, and was renamed Presidency College in 1855. (हिंदू कॉलेज, 1817 — कोलकाता)

 

• It was established largely through the efforts of Raja Rammohan Roy, David Hare and Sir Edward Hyde East, to impart modern Western education in English to the sons of the Bengali gentry.

 

• It became the intellectual centre of the Bengal Renaissance. Henry Louis Vivian Derozio taught there and inspired the radical Young Bengal Movement. Its alumni include Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, Swami Vivekananda, Subhas Chandra Bose, Satyendra Nath Bose, Jagadish Chandra Bose and Amartya Sen.

 

• It was converted into Presidency University in 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Landmark institutions of colonial education:
◦ Calcutta Madrasa (1781) — founded by Warren Hastings
◦ Asiatic Society of Bengal (1784) — Sir William Jones
◦ Sanskrit College, Banaras (1791) — Jonathan Duncan
◦ Fort William College (1800) — Lord Wellesley
◦ Hindu College, Calcutta (1817)
◦ Elphinstone College, Bombay (1856)
◦ The Universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras (1857), set up on the recommendation of Wood's Despatch (1854), called the Magna Carta of English education in India

 

• Macaulay's Minute (1835) settled the Orientalist-Anglicist controversy in favour of English education, and the Hunter Commission (1882) reviewed primary and secondary education.

 

NOTE

 

• Chennai (Option 2): Site of Presidency College, Madras, founded in 1840 — a different institution with a similar name.

 

• Mumbai (Option 3): Site of Elphinstone College, founded in 1856.

 

• Varanasi (Option 4): Site of the Sanskrit College (1791) and the Banaras Hindu University (1916), founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya.

question: 'Mando', a traditional form of song and dance performed at weddings and festive occasions, belongs to which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mando is a traditional song-and-dance form of Goa, sung in the Konkani language and performed at weddings and festive gatherings. (मांडो — गोवा)

 

• It developed in the nineteenth century among the Goan Catholic community and reflects a blend of Indian and Portuguese musical traditions. It is slow and dignified in tempo, dealing with themes of love, longing and social life, and is accompanied by the violin, guitar and the ghumot, a traditional Goan percussion instrument.

 

• The dance is performed by men and women in facing rows, the women holding fans, and it is typically followed by the faster Dulpod.

 

• Other folk forms of Goa: Dekhni, Fugdi, Dhalo, Corridinho, Ghode Modni and Talgadi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

question: Which Indian freedom fighter was popularly known as 'Lokmanya'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1856-1920) was popularly known as "Lokmanya", meaning "accepted by the people as their leader". (लोकमान्य — बाल गंगाधर तिलक)

 

• He is remembered for the declaration "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it", and the British called him the "Father of the Indian Unrest".

 

• He was one of the trio "Lal-Bal-Pal" — Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal — the leaders of the Extremist (Garam Dal) group, which parted from the Moderates at the Surat Split of 1907.

 

• He founded the newspapers Kesari (Marathi) and Maratha (English), started the Ganapati (1893) and Shivaji (1895) festivals to build national feeling, and established the All India Home Rule League in 1916 at Belgaum. He wrote "Gita Rahasya" and "The Arctic Home in the Vedas" while imprisoned at Mandalay.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

• Bipin Chandra Pal (Option 3): The "Pal" of Lal-Bal-Pal, called the "Father of Revolutionary Thoughts".
